LanguageData.RuleCore.EnableLogDesc: When off, only errors are recorded. Errors are always recorded.
LanguageData.RuleCore.VerboseLogDesc: Record every detection evaluation, not just hits and failures.
LanguageData.RuleCore.LogToFileDesc: Mirror the timeline into log/*.md inside the mod folder, so it survives the session and can be shared.
LanguageData.RuleCore.LogFileFailed: File output: failed to start, memory only (see Player.log)
LanguageData.RuleCore.Panel.Title: RuleCore
LanguageData.RuleCore.Panel.NoSelection: Click a row to select it first.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Panel.Missing: Could not find the RuleCore panel — its Defs probably failed to load.

LanguageData.RuleCore.Form.NoSelection:
Click a rule on the left and it is laid out in three parts: subject / detection / operations.
(This build is read-only inspection — first we settle what a sentence should look like, then make every word clickable.)
LanguageData.RuleCore.Inspect.Subject: Subject
LanguageData.RuleCore.Inspect.NoSubject: no subject binding (evaluated once for the map)
LanguageData.RuleCore.NewRuleDesc: A freshly created rule. It only writes a log line — it reads nothing and touches nothing, so you cannot break anything by clicking around.
LanguageData.RuleCore.NewRuleActionText: This is a player rule: if you can still see it after restarting the game, rules really do make it into the config.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Subject.freeColonistsDesc: Run the rule once per free colonist on the map. Cooldowns and loop detection are tracked per pawn too — one pawn firing must not spend another pawn's budget.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.outdoorTempDesc: Outdoor temperature of the map, in Celsius.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.weatherDesc: The current weather type: Clear / Rain / Thunderstorm, plus anything mods add.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.colonistCountDesc: Spawned free colonists on this map (caravans away from home do not count).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.rainRateDesc: 0 means no rain, 1 means heavy rain. Use "greater than 0" for "is it raining", "greater than 0.5" for "is it pouring".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.snowRateDesc: 0 means no snow, 1 means heavy snow.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.healthDesc: Overall health, 1 being unharmed (the bar at the top of the vanilla health tab).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.positionDesc: The cell they are standing on.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.locationTempDesc: Their own warmth: room temperature indoors, outdoor temperature outside. The two should be continuous — stepping through a doorway should not make the reading jump.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.apparelDesc: Everything they are wearing (a group). Because it yields a group, a reduction must follow: `.Count` asks how many, `.First` picks one to read further.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.shelterCellDesc: The nearest standable roofed cell that is actually reachable. A deterministic scan — the same world state always resolves to the same cell, so saves and replays do not drift.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.thing.durabilityDesc: Remaining durability as a fraction, 1 being pristine. Inside a filter this reads as "durability less than 50%".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.thing.defNameDesc: The defName of the thing — how "is this a hat" gets answered.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.compare.gtDesc: Number comparison. Stays true while it keeps holding (level).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.compare.ltDesc: Number comparison. Stays true while it keeps holding (level).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.compare.eqDesc: With a float tolerance (0.0001). Readings like temperature are nudged every tick, so exact equality is unreliable.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.compare.neDesc: The complement of "equal to", sharing the same tolerance.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.match.isDesc: Name comparison: is the current value this one. Which word shows up in the dropdown depends on what the subject yields — numbers get "equal to", names get "is".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.state.alwaysDesc: Always true. Use it for purely periodic rules ("do this every N ticks") or just to confirm the engine is running.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.state.idleDesc: This pawn is free right now (wandering counts). When false the rule stands down quietly: no interrupting hauling, building or cooking, and it is not a rule failure.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.state.ableDesc: Not downed, not in a mental break, not drafted, still mobile. When false the rule stands down quietly. It does interrupt current work — a raid should interrupt work.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.event.letterDesc: A letter of this type arrived recently — the moment a red letter pops up and the game pauses, i.e. when the player realises something happened. It is edge semantics implemented as a time window: detection lags up to one sample step (250 ticks, about 4 seconds), and dismissing the letter inside the window suppresses it.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.op.logDesc: Write one entry to the timeline. Changes nothing — the simplest way to prove a rule is actually being evaluated.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.op.gotoDesc: Send the actor walking to a cell. Issues one job and lets go — pathing and anything on the way belong to vanilla AI. If vanilla refuses (drafted, higher-priority job) the rule stands down: vanilla comes first.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.op.removeApparelDesc: Remove one worn item from the actor. Developer tier: vanilla has no job for undressing a conscious pawn (JobDefOf.Strip only works on corpses and downed pawns), so this has to change world state directly. What vanilla will not do for you, you do yourself.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.map.setWeatherDesc: Switch the weather to another type ("the map becomes rain"). Developer tier: this changes world state directly rather than delegating to someone.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.map.incidentDesc: Fire a vanilla incident (raid, solar flare, toxic fallout, eclipse, wanderers join...). It goes **through vanilla's incident system**, so the incident's own duration, letter, difficulty limits, "fired too recently" and scenario bans all still apply; if vanilla says it cannot happen now, the operation quietly stands down instead of forcing it. Developer tier.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.map.sendLetterDesc: Pop a letter telling the player what happened. For starting a game condition, use Trigger incident — vanilla conditions ARE incidents and their duration lives on the incident (IncidentDef.durationDays); registering a GameCondition yourself could only guess. Player tier.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.map.hasConditionDesc: Whether a persistent condition is currently active on this map (eclipse, toxic fallout, cold snap, psychic drone). It is the read side of Trigger incident: start it with one, watch it with the other.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.GodDeniedHint: The actions tagged "not granted" above will not take effect. To allow them: mod settings → "指令核心 RuleCore" → tick "Allow developer-tier operations".
LanguageData.RuleCore.AllowDeveloperOpsDesc: Lets rules change world state directly: set weather, trigger incidents. These are powerful, so this is off by default and it is your call. Note it only decides whether they are allowed — a rule made of player-tier actions does not become developer-tier because of it.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.GroupRootHint: "All {0}" is one whole group. It can only be **counted** (.count) or **picked apart** (.first) — you cannot read a property off it, because "the energy of this group" is not a value. To have **each {0} judged on its own energy / its own position**, change the **subject binding** at the top to "{0}": the whole rule then runs once per member, and each one only sees its own numbers.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.hourDesc: Current local hour (0-23). For "is it daytime" use "Is daytime"; for a precise window use this, e.g. "at least 6 and less than 18".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.isDayDesc: Astronomical daytime by local time (6:00-18:00), **independent of weather and eclipses**. For "how bright is it right now" use "Sky glow" — an eclipse drops that. Keeping them apart is what makes "outdoors and daytime and sky glow above 0.3" writable.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.outdoorDesc: There is no roof over his head. **It answers "is there a roof", not "is it bright"** — that is what "sky glow" is for. Mechanoids have no outdoors need, so this asks the roof grid directly, and it works the same for humans and animals.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.op.chargeDesc: Push the executor's energy up (percentage, 1 = 100%). Vanilla charging happens at a mech charger; this changes the energy directly, so it is developer tier. Already full counts as "already satisfied" rather than an error.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.ReadOnlyHint: Built-in rules are read-only. Create your own rule to change things.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Section.Subject: Subject
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Field.Name: Name
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Subject.NoneHint: evaluated once for the map; anything reading the subject is always false
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoOperate: No operations, so this rule does nothing.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NotEmpty: NOT is empty — give it a detection.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NothingToAppend: This path is at its end.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoReduce: No reduction applies here (this is already a single value).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.EnumNeedsTyping: This predicate declares no value domain, so it has to be typed.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoValueDomain: No selectable values (this vocabulary entry declares no Def type).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.TooManyValues: …too many candidates, only the first 60 are listed.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.UnsupportedArg: The editor does not support {0} arguments yet.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Root.Subject: the subject
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Root.SubjectDesc: The actor of this evaluation. The rule runs once per bound subject.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Root.ElementDesc: The item a filter is walking. Only meaningful inside a filter.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Root.MapDesc: The map being evaluated. The engine is instantiated per map, so the rule runs once per map.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Root.ColonistsDesc: Everyone on the map (a group). A reduction must follow.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Root.AllMapsDesc: Every map (a group). A reduction must follow.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.skyGlowDesc: 0-1: near 1 in daylight, near 0 at night, continuous through dusk. Use "less than 0.3" for "it is getting dark".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.wealthDesc: Total value of everything on this map.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.moodDesc: Mood need as a fraction, 1 being satisfied. Unreadable on mechanoids, which have no mood.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.foodDesc: Food need as a fraction, 1 being full.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.restDesc: Rest need as a fraction, 1 being fully rested.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.isDraftedDesc: Whether the player has taken this pawn over. A boolean fact — pair it with "is true".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.isDownedDesc: Whether they are down on the ground. A boolean fact — pair it with "is true".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.roomDesc: The room they are in. Unreadable outdoors — that is "no room", not "a room of zero", and conflating the two makes room checks silently true outside.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.room.temperatureDesc: Temperature inside the room, in Celsius.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.room.cellCountDesc: How many cells the room has. "Less than 20" means cramped.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.thing.hitPointsDesc: Absolute hit points (not a fraction). Use "durability" for the fraction.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.state.holdsDesc: Use a boolean fact as a detection. With this, facts like "drafted" or "downed" do not each need their own predicate — adding a fact is adding a property row.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Picker.Title: Pick: {0}
LanguageData.RuleCore.Picker.NoMatch: Nothing matches. Try another word — defName and label both work.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Section.Path: Entity path (click a segment to cut back to it)
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.bedDesc: The bed he has **claimed as his own**. Unclaimed (or no ownership record) means it cannot be read — not "reads as empty", the check stands down. To write "go to bed", append a cell: `本主体.床位.交互格`.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.thing.interactionCellDesc: The cell others stand on to use this thing (vanilla `Thing.InteractionCell`). This is the honest source for "go somewhere" — **the cell really exists in the game**. Off-map things can't produce one.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Section.Quantify: What is this group like (each element judged separately)
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.QuantifyHint: The reductions above **pick one out** (how many / which one); this **asks one question about the whole group** and yields true or false. E.g. "every hat has durability below 50%" = apparel, all of them satisfy (durability < 50%). Note: **on an empty group both "all satisfy" and "none satisfy" hold** — "I have no hats" really does mean "all my hats are fine".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.medCareDesc: The medical care level set on the Assign tab (no care / no meds / herbal or worse / normal or worse / best). Use it with "is".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.hostilityResponseDesc: Automatic reaction when attacked (ignore / attack / flee). Use it with "is".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.areaDesc: The area he is currently restricted to ("unrestricted" is a value too). Areas are **drawn by you in game**, so the candidates are read live — the same rule points at different ids in another save.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.outfitDesc: The apparel policy he uses (the Assign column). Policies are player-made, so candidates are read live.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.foodPolicyDesc: The food restriction he uses. Player-made, so candidates are read live.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.drugPolicyDesc: The drug policy he uses. Player-made, so candidates are read live.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.timetableDesc: What his current hour is scheduled as (sleep / work / joy...). **Read-only** — a timetable is a 24-slot table, not a single value.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.pawn.setMedCareDesc: Change the executor's medical care level. Player tier.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.pawn.setHostilityResponseD: Change the executor's hostility response. Player tier.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.pawn.setAreaDesc: Restrict the executor to an area (or "unrestricted" to free him). Player tier. **He must be on a map** — vanilla silently does nothing otherwise; this reports the failure honestly.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.pawn.setOutfitDesc: Change the executor's apparel policy. Player tier.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.pawn.setFoodPolicyDesc: Change the executor's food restriction. Player tier.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Verb.pawn.setDrugPolicyDesc: Change the executor's drug policy. Player tier.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoRuntimeOption: Nothing to choose from yet — areas and policies are things you create in game; make one on the Assign/Restrict tab first.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Section.RawKey: No value source declared here — you must type a defName
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.ClauseEmpty: No clauses yet — use the buttons below.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.InspectorHint: Click any slot in the sentence to start editing. The options for that slot show up here — no popup covering the sentence.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoVerbForType: No predicate applies to this subject type.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.PathEnd: This path is at its end.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.BrokenPath: The path has an unknown key (hand-edited XML?).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.MoreItems: …only the first 200 are listed; use "search all" above for the rest
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoneUsableAfterFilter: {0} candidates are registered, but none of them is usable under the current conditions (e.g. the incident does not target a map). Pick another verb or another object.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoCandidateAtAll: Could not read the candidate list for "{0}" — this is a lookup failure, not "nothing to choose from". Logged to the timeline.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.PickOneHint: Click the row above to pick a value. The candidates are vanilla's full list (mods included); when there are many it opens a window you can type into.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Section.Subject: Subject binding (who "the subject" is)
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Subject.Hint: With no subject binding the engine evaluates the rule once for the map — and any detection reading "the subject" is then always false.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NeedBinding: This clause reads the subject, but the rule has no subject binding yet — pick one in the bar at the top.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.PickRootHint: Pick a root above first, then read properties off it.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.BindFirst: ⚠ This rule has no subject binding — click here to pick one
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NeedsReduceFirst: A group is not something a predicate can act on. Go back a level and add a reduction first (.count to count, .first to take one), then come back.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Subject.prisonersDesc: Runs the rule once per colony prisoner on the map. Cooldowns and loop detection are per person — one prisoner firing must not consume another's turn.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Subject.slavesDesc: Runs the rule once per colony slave on the map. A slave is also a colony member, but when the question is "who is he", the situation outranks the membership.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Subject.colonyMechsDesc: Runs the rule once per player-owned mechanoid on the map. They have no food need, only energy — pick this and "food" disappears from the property list.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Subject.colonyAnimalsDesc: Runs the rule once per player-owned animal on the map. Animals have no ideoligion and cannot be drafted, so those options never show up for them.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Subject.guestsDesc: Runs the rule once per pawn who is hosted but is neither a prisoner nor a slave: visiting caravans, refugees, deserters.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Subject.namedPawnDesc: Runs the whole rule once, for that one named pawn, and writes his name straight into the sentence. Once you have named him, "what he is" no longer needs judging inside the rule — the editor just tells you. One honest limitation: player rules live in global config while a pawn reference is issued per save, so in another save he cannot be found and the rule will not fire (the editor says so).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.energyDesc: A mechanoid's charge level, 1 = full. This is the mechanoid's "food" — the same slot meaning the same thing, just a different name and a different need object. Mechanoids list this one instead of food.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.ageDesc: Biological age in years. "He is still a child" is `less than 16`.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.pawn.equipmentDesc: The thing in his primary hand. Empty hands read as unavailable, not as "holding an empty thing" — conflating the two would make `Held weapon.durability less than 50%` silently true while empty-handed.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.prisonerCountDesc: Spawned colony prisoners on this map (those away on caravans do not count).
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.slaveCountDesc: Spawned colony slaves on this map.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.colonyMechCountDesc: Spawned player-owned mechanoids on this map.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.colonyAnimalCountDesc: Spawned player-owned animals on this map.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Prop.map.pawnCountDesc: Every spawned pawn on this map, hostiles and animals included. This is how you ask "how big was that raid, really".
LanguageData.RuleCore.Cap.Bed: the ability to own a bed
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Section.SubjectGroup: or, run it once per member of a class
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Section.NotForThis: Not usable here (the current subject lacks what they need)
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Subject.NamedHint: The rule runs once, for the pawn you name, and the sentence uses his name. Once he is named, "what he is" no longer needs judging inside the rule.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Subject.MissingHint: "{0}" cannot be found in this save. Player rules live in global config while a pawn reference is issued per save — in another save he is gone and this rule will not fire.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Subject.GroupIdentityHint: The binding IS the identity: bind "prisoners" and everyone in that run is a prisoner — no need to also write "he is a prisoner". The property list follows too: a mechanoid has no food, only energy.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Subject.NoMember: No subjects matched this tick (nobody on the map fits), so the rule will not run.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.Subject.NoCandidate: There is nobody on this map to name.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.BackToSentence: Once you are done here, click any slot in the sentence to keep editing subject / predicate / object.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.NoWayToMake: Nothing in the vocabulary produces "{0}" right now — you need a mod to add a row, or reword this rule so it does not need one.
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.ObjectTypeBad: ⚠ this verb wants "{0}", but the path currently yields "{1}"
LanguageData.RuleCore.Edit.VerbNoLongerValid: "{0}" no longer applies: its subject is now "{1}" — pick a new predicate above.
